nodes.question: Comparing the same jacket in the source and edited images, what progress toward closing it is visibly evident?
nodes.criteria: complete: the jacket is fully closed, with its front edges meeting or overlapping along the opening and no substantial inner layer exposed. partial: the edited jacket is visibly more closed than in the source, such as front edges moving closer together or less inner layer exposed, but it remains partly open. absent: there is no visible progress toward closing the jacket compared with the source, or it is equally or more open. unknown: the jacket, its opening, or the source-to-edit comparison is too occluded, low-resolution, or otherwise unclear to determine progress or completion.
nodes.binding: Visual target: the woman's jacket. Compare its visible front opening and exposed inner layer in the source and edited images; do not infer closure from pose or jacket movement alone.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
